reviewer: ChatGPT — author-side commander-first strategic assessment, NOT independent formal Pass C
reviewed_source: approved exact canonically locked lists and M6 blueprints/review-packets

reviews.existing_strategic_role: One-mana Faithless Looting filters two cards while loading spells/recursion resources into the graveyard, has flashback, and is a sorcery payable from Cormela's restricted UBR when her ability is available.
reviews.added_strategic_role: Four-mana Archaeomancer returns one instant or sorcery from graveyard to hand on creature entry, but adds a sorcery-speed creature to a fast ritual/storm shell and redundantly overlaps Cormela's death trigger.
commander_specific_rules: Cormela's {1}, {T} mana restriction allows only instant and/or sorcery casts; that generated UBR cannot cast Archaeomancer because it is a creature.

Archaeomancer's ETB trigger, unlike Cormela's death trigger, requires the Archaeomancer permanent to resolve and survive to trigger; repeated recursion needs an additional blink or recursion mechanism.
Removing Faithless Looting also eliminates its cheap flashback discard outlet and graveyard setup. The M5 report's extra Spellbook combos do not demonstrate accessible turn/tempo performance.
reviews.why_no_change: The proposed exchange raises minimum mana for basic spell selection and does not replace a unique commander loop; the plausible graveyard spell return is less compelling at Cormela's documented cEDH ceiling than instant-speed/lower-cost chain support.
missing_evidence: Proven effect-legal commander-specific Archaeomancer recursion that beats the current Cormela loops in actual 100-card hands.
Tempo/turn-to-assemble comparison with creature mana unavailable from Cormela's restricted mana.
Independent Pass C review and actual current-time rules/legality plus exact full deck verification before any proposed approval.
reviews.next_action: Do not remove Faithless Looting for this candidate. Investigate only if a demonstrated new commander-centered line requires Archaeomancer at acceptable tempo.

reviews.existing_strategic_role: One-black-mana Dockside Chef has {1}{B}, sacrifice an artifact or creature as a cost: draw a card. Ashnod copies the nonmana ability when the cost sacrifices a permanent, resulting in two draws from one activation/sacrifice if Ashnod is present.
reviews.added_strategic_role: Four-mana Detective's Satchel investigates twice on entry to produce two Clues. Each Clue has {2}, sacrifice this artifact as activation cost to draw; Ashnod copies the Clue's ability, but Satchel's own {T} Thopter-token activation has no sacrifice in its activation cost and is not copied.
commander_specific_rules: Ashnod has no once-per-turn limit and can copy qualifying artifact/creature nonmana activated abilities whose own activation cost sacrifices a permanent. A sacrifice made earlier that turn to unlock another card's {T} ability does not make that later ability eligible.

Chef's activated sacrifice cost qualifies for Ashnod; its one sacrificed artifact/creature can draw two total cards with Ashnod present (original and copy), subject to the spell/permanent remaining in play as relevant.

Satchel-created Clues qualify individually because each Clue's activation cost sacrifices itself. Satchel's Thopter generation itself does not qualify and typically costs untapping the Satchel between activations.
No evidence was supplied that four-mana Clue provisioning compensates for removing the cheaper repeatable Chef sacrifice engine in the current recursion/cost-focused 100.
reviews.why_no_change: The proposed add has legitimate Clue/Ashnod synergy, but sacrifices a cheap repeatable commander-copyable outlet for a higher-cost, finite source of Clues and an independently uncopyable Satchel tap ability. The M5 'test_pass' cannot resolve that value difference.
missing_evidence: Controlled costed comparison of Chef-activated double draws versus Satchel's finite copyable Clue draws and Thopter fuel.
Proper turn-by-turn modeling of sacrifice fodder, artifacts returning, summoning sickness/tap sequencing, and Ashnod in play.
Independent Pass C and source-bound full-deck audit of any future alternative cut.
reviews.next_action: Retain Dockside Chef. Investigate Detective's Satchel only as a separate candidate against a demonstrably weaker slot, and account for both mana and sacrifice-cost timing.

reviews.existing_strategic_role: Opposition Agent has flash and replaces opponents' library searches with controlled searches and card exiling/possible card access. It is proactive interaction against tutor-heavy opponents, even though it does not enable Gwendlyn's activation.
reviews.added_strategic_role: Aphetto Alchemist costs {1}{U}, taps to untap a target artifact or creature; can untap Gwendlyn for another random-discard activation on the active player's turn after Alchemist itself is able to tap.
commander_specific_rules: Gwendlyn's random-discard {T} activation is only legal during its controller's turn and obeys summoning sickness. She needs to survive and be untapped to use it.
Alchemist's own {T} requires it to be able to tap; it can target Gwendlyn, but shroud granted by Pemmin's Aura prevents targeting Gwendlyn with Alchemist's activated ability.

Illusionist's Bracers equips to one creature at a time. When equipped to Alchemist, the Alchemist tap ability can be copied, with one target the Alchemist and the other target Gwendlyn; this can enable repeated Gwendlyn untaps only while legal targets/turn and survival conditions hold. It does not simultaneously copy Gwendlyn's discard ability if Bracers was moved off Gwendlyn.
Repeated random discard cannot be scored as an infinite win: opponents have finite cards in hand, and discard payoff timing plus reloading wheels and interactions must be modeled.
The M5 combo completion annotation does not establish the relative value of losing Opposition Agent's opponent-search control in a high-power multiplayer environment.
reviews.why_no_change: Alchemist fits the commander-first plan substantially better than a generic card, but sacrificing unique powerful tutor denial is consequential. The accepted approved deck already has Minamo, Magewright's Stone, Patriar's Seal, Thousand-Year Elixir and Pemmin's Aura; another untapper may be welcome or redundant depending on availability and matchup.
missing_evidence: Rules-grounded activation sequencing for Gwendlyn + Alchemist, with/without Bracers equipped to each and with/without Pemmin shroud.
Turn-to-discard and actual opposing-hand count payoff across paired openings, including summoning sickness and removal risk.
Opponent search/tutor denial opportunity cost of cutting Opposition Agent, realistic interaction density and alternate lower-cost potential cuts.
Named independent strategic critique, Phase B and owner approval if any real swap becomes justified.
reviews.next_action: Shortlist Aphetto Alchemist as genuine identity-positive candidate, but do not cut Opposition Agent without targeted benefit-versus-disruption evidence. Retain current list.
